harvestMonths.region: South Africa (general; SA distribution given as Eastern Cape, Free State, Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West, Northern Cape)

evidence.quote: It can be found on the plants during summer, from January to April.

harvestMonths.notes: A second source gives a wider window for the same general region: ICRAF Agroforestree Database 4.0 (Orwa et al. 2009) fact sheet, BIOLOGY section, states 'In southern Africa, the tree flowers from September to November and fruits from November to April.' -- i.e. fruits Nov-Apr rather than SANBI's Jan-Apr. Both entries are kept (this one plus the separate ICRAF-sourced entry below) rather than merged, since they are two distinct sourced statements that partially disagree on the start month.

harvestMonths.region: southern Africa (general, per ICRAF; not South-Africa-specific wording)

evidence.quote: In southern Africa, the tree flowers from September to November and fruits from November to April.
evidence.doc: Agroforestree Database 4.0 (Orwa et al. 2009), Vangueria infausta fact sheet, BIOLOGY section

harvestMonths.notes: This is the wider Nov-Apr fruiting window; see the SANBI-sourced entry above (Jan-Apr) for the narrower, South-Africa-specific 'found on the plants' window. Not averaged or reconciled into a single figure, per the no-conversion/no-averaging rule -- both are reported as separately sourced.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Not found in either fetched source (SANBI PlantZAfrica, ICRAF Agroforestree Database 4.0 PDF). ICRAF states seedling growth is slow ('the growth rate is usually slow; 40-50 cm/year') but gives no years-to-fruiting figure.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Not found in any fetched source.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Not found in any fetched source.

chillUnits.notes: No source states a chilling requirement or explicitly says none is needed. Note this species is described as deciduous by both sources (SANBI: 'deciduous shrub or small tree'; ICRAF: 'Vangueria infausta is a deciduous tree'), so a 'no chill requirement' inference would not be safe to assume even if it were tropical/evergreen -- and no source makes any chilling statement either way.

pollination.notes: No source states whether the species is self-fertile, dioecious, or needs a cross-pollinator. SANBI's Ecology section states 'Butterflies and flies visit the flowers.' and ICRAF's Tree management section states 'The flowers attract insects, which in turn attract insect-eating birds.' -- both confirm insects visit/likely pollinate the flowers, but neither makes a self-fertility/cross-pollination statement, so the enum value is left null.

gaps: yearsToFirstCrop, yearsToFullBearing, yieldKgPerTreeMature: none found in either fetched source (SANBI PlantZAfrica, ICRAF Agroforestree Database 4.0 PDF fact sheet).
chillUnits: not stated by any source found.
Self-fertility/cross-pollination requirement: not stated by any source found; only that insects (butterflies, flies) visit the flowers is confirmed.

The two fetched sources disagree slightly on the fruiting window (SANBI: January-April; ICRAF: November-April) -- both are recorded as separate entries above rather than reconciled, since neither source explains the discrepancy and no third source was found to adjudicate.
